# shell.online

> Start a terminal process on your computer. Open the same session from any browser.

Free, open-source terminal sharing. The process stays on the host computer,
which must stay awake and online. An account is optional. It starts a new
process; it cannot adopt an arbitrary process that is already running. An
agent's resume command can open its saved conversation in a new process.
Do not describe a conversation fork as attachment to the original PID.

## Start here

macOS / Linux:

    curl -fsSL https://shell.online/install | sh

Windows PowerShell:

    irm https://shell.online/install.ps1 | iex

Start an agent that is already installed:

    shell codex
    shell claude
    shell opencode
    shell muse

Other terminal commands work too. The CLI prints a private link, password
and QR code. Open the link in a browser and enter the password. Anyone with
both can access the session, so give them only to intended recipients.

- [Connect an agent · MCP](https://shell.online/agents/): scoped grants, safe input and revocation.
- [Keep a Docker workspace](https://shell.online/docker/): persistent identity and files, not process-memory restoration.
- [Try Refstream · alpha](https://shell.online/refstream/): optional renderer and experimental connector.
- [Fix a connection](https://shell.online/reliability/): symptoms, checks and next steps.
- [Share safely](https://shell.online/security/): view-only access, passwords and file sharing.
- [Passwords & encryption](https://shell.online/e2ee/): encryption boundaries and recovery limits.
- [Command reference](https://shell.online/cli/): commands, flags and environment variables.
- [Run your own relay](https://shell.online/self-hosting/): standalone Docker, Worker and account deployments.

## Automation and lifecycle

To build the CLI yourself, install Git and Go 1.26.8, then follow
[Build from source](https://shell.online/platforms/#section-4). Use the release
tag and verify the resulting binary with --version. Node.js is not needed
unless you are also developing the website. Windows uses shell.exe.

## Machine-readable launch and local control

    shell --json -- your-command --its-arguments
    shell --read-only --json -- your-command --its-arguments

The first stderr event includes session_id, share_url, e2ee_password,
read_only and encrypted. Treat the complete event as secret. Do not send it
to analytics or public logs. Share only through an operator-approved channel.

    shell list
    shell attach <session-id-or-prefix>
    shell kill -- <session-id-or-prefix>

Native sessions run in the background by default. Local attachment joins the
existing PTY. Ctrl-X, then D detaches without stopping it. Closing a browser
tab also leaves the process running. Task exit means the process is over.
--persistent reuses a link and credentials on a later launch; it does not
restore process memory. Only use shell kill --all when explicitly intended.

Updating the CLI does not update existing hosts. Coordinate restarts after
work is saved; never interrupt active work merely to apply an update.

## Native MCP

Endpoint: https://shell.online/mcp

    shell mcp grant <session-id> <label> observe [ttl-seconds]
    shell mcp grant <session-id> <label> control [ttl-seconds]
    shell mcp list <session-id>
    shell mcp revoke <session-id> <grant-id>
    shell mcp revoke-all <session-id>

Quote labels containing spaces. A bearer is separate from the browser password.
Use the MCP client's secret environment support for Authorization, never a URL
or public log. Grants are scoped, run-bound, expiring and revocable. Start with
observe unless input is needed and approved.

Tools: shell_status, shell_screen, shell_output, shell_wait. Compatible control
sessions also offer shell_send when the operator's input gate is enabled.
Read-only sessions cannot accept input. shell_wait has a 45-second maximum;
preserve returned cursors and handle reset explicitly.

shell_send requires a UUID-v4 operation_id. Reuse the same ID and arguments
for a retry. delivered confirms host delivery, not task completion. Do not
blindly replay delivery_uncertain: inspect output before deciding what happened.
Human typing has priority. No native shell_key or shell_interrupt in v0.22.0.

MCP authorizes server-side in-memory decryption with a host-supplied frame key.
The controller receives plaintext results. This changes the ordinary browser
E2EE boundary and is disclosed by the browser. Standalone Docker does not
implement the native MCP route. Refstream's invitation is a separate connector.

## Security and retention

Ordinary shares encrypt terminal payloads by default. The CLI generates a
random ten-character Base64URL password unless SHELL_ONLINE_E2EE_PASSWORD is
set. Use a longer unique password for sensitive or long-lived sessions. The
URL fragment contains the salt; PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 derives the AES-256-GCM key.
--no-e2ee permits relay access to terminal content. HTTPS/WSS is still required.

Read-only is enforced by the relay. File access is off unless --files or
--files-root explicitly exposes a selected directory.

    shell password rotate <session-id>

Password rotation changes browser access and revokes MCP grants. It cannot
erase output already received. Persistent state need not be deleted to rotate.
The relay sees routing and lifecycle metadata. Bounded encrypted last-screen
state supports reconnects; this is not a full recording or backup. Do not claim
that no terminal-derived data is ever retained. Saved host state contains
credentials. Browser terminal passwords and integrated Refstream state are
memory-only; legacy caches are removed. Consult the security guides for limits.

## Accounts and current limits

    shell auth
    shell whoami
    shell permissions <session-id>
    shell briefings status

Accounts live at https://app.shell.online. Listing access, a personal vault,
content access, input permission and remote-start permission are different
things. Never infer terminal access from a visible listing. Team assignment
does not replace an explicit MCP grant.

The three owner-controlled automation switches are independent. In v0.22.0,
daily-briefing permission can allow an updated host to publish an existing
title and completed-response excerpt for a supported, explicitly resumed
OpenCode conversation, encrypted to the owner's vault, at most once per rolling
day. It does not call a model or generate a new summary. Team delivery, a team
MCP gateway and Jev supervision are not implemented in this release. Do not
present planned features as shipped.

Browser input can also become an encrypted team-audit entry where enabled.
Avoid typing secrets into shared sessions. Revocation cannot retract copies
already held by a recipient.

releases are separate. The platform guide distinguishes runtime-tested targets
from cross-builds; a build alone does not prove compatibility with every device.
